activity.title: Last week, I competed at Carnegie Mellon’s Build18, a week-long hardware hackathon. My team took inspiration from the robot boxing movie Real Steel and built ShadowControl: a humanoid robot that copies your upper-body movements in real time. The idea was simple: stand in front of a camera, move your arms, and the robot mirrors you like a “robot puppeteer.” What wasn’t simple was getting it all to behave 😅. We built the whole thing together, from wiring and setup to a software pipeline that uses Google MediaPipe for pose detection and drives the robot’s joints in real time. Watching it finally move smoothly was definitely the highlight of the week! You can find our demo on the project page link below. Big shoutout to my teammates Rohan Nagabhirava , Abhishek Hemlani , Madhavan Iyengar , and Revanth Krishna Senthilkumaran , and to Build18 for funding our project and organizing an incredible event! Project page: https://lnkd.in/eyeexTUD Repo: https://lnkd.in/eMp7WnWV #Build18 #CMU #Robotics #Humanoids #ComputerVision ...more

I won my first hackathon! And… did my first-ever comedy gig???! (for 400+ people 😵) This weekend, I competed at TartanHacks at Carnegie Mellon! Despite having helped organize 3 university hackathons, this was my first time on the participant side. It was really an amazing experience. My teammates and I (not pictured since they all dipped before the closing ceremony 🤡 - Ganesh Selvakumar , Lucas Ribaudo , and Johnny Kretzing ), have been roommates for 3 years now. We know the struggle of managing dishes, chores, and expenses all too well. So over 24 hours, we built Roomiez, an all-in-one platform to make roommate life easier. Check out our short demo: https://lnkd.in/dDjk7-PQ Roomiez is also live at localhost:3000 if anyone wants to check it out 😉 Despite this being our all of our first real hackathon, we won Best Non-AI Project out of 176 total projects! We all won Polaroid cameras 🤩 Oh, and in a crazy twist - I did 20 minutes of stand-up with Jeremy Luu for a 400-person crowd at the event… with zero prep. While waiting for the deliberation to end, we suggested to the organizers to let us entertain the crowd. And the rest is history. If you were there, I hope we made you laugh! DM us if you want us to perform at your birthday party!! Huge shoutout to ScottyLabs for an incredible event. The organizers all absolutely killed it, and made it a ton of fun. Couldn’t have asked for a better hackathon experience! ...more ...more

It's been almost a year since Rohan and I started RapidEye. This journey has been incredible! Here's what happened, in the order it happened: Before 2024: While managing his own vacation rentals, Rohan Nagabhirava realized he couldn't keep track of all the items in his house. Cleaners didn't remember where things were. Early 2025: While working at Rivian and Lucid Motors on their computer vision pipelines, he realized he could solve this issue with AI. Mid 2025: At the same time, I was experimenting with the frontier of VLMs at ValueMate (YC X25) . I realized this technology was revolutionary and wanted to bring it to another market. Late 2025: Rohan and I teamed up to create an early prototype of RapidEye . It worked! December 2025: First big (200+ unit) customers. We learned so much from them. Product really started working. January 2026: Really realizing this is a huge opportunity, learning what channels worked for marketing. Went all in, more large customers. March 2026: We win $50,000 at the Carnegie Mellon University McGinnis Venture Competition. Oh sh*t moment May 2026: We moved to SF. We continued to scale 😂 Now: We're pushing as hard as we can to make RapidEye better for all of our existing customers. Hopefully you've seen how many improvements I've posted here on LinkedIn in the past months. Every single step was way harder than it sounds writing it out, and that's why it was worth it :) Excited to keep pushing 🚀 - sam

✨ 𝐀 𝐧𝐞𝐰 𝐭𝐲𝐩𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐭𝐨𝐮𝐜𝐡 𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐚 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐦𝐚𝐲 𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐠𝐚𝐦𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐫𝐨𝐛𝐨𝐭𝐢𝐜 𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐚 𝐜𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧. Nearly every tactile sensor today infers contact from surface deformation, and that assumption costs us three ways: it goes blind on 𝐟𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐢𝐥𝐞, 𝐥𝐢𝐪𝐮𝐢𝐝, or 𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐥𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐨𝐛𝐣𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐬 right at the moment contact begins; it demands 𝐜𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐛𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 redone for every mechanical design that may not transfer from one to anther; and the format might not be compatible to vision-language 𝐟𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐦𝐨𝐝𝐞𝐥s. Today we 🔥 𝐨𝐩𝐞𝐧-𝐬𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐜𝐞 🔥 𝐋𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐭𝐓𝐚𝐜𝐭, our new 𝐑𝐒𝐒 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔 paper 🚀 — a visual-tactile fingertip sensor that makes contact 𝐝𝐢𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐥𝐲 𝐯𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐛𝐥𝐞, no deformation required. Its 𝐚𝐦𝐛𝐢𝐞𝐧𝐭-𝐛𝐥𝐨𝐜𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐨𝐩𝐭𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐥 𝐝𝐞𝐬𝐢𝐠𝐧 suppresses both external and internal light everywhere except at true contact points, where scattered light leaks through. Contact stops being a 𝐦𝐞𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐧𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐥 inference problem and becomes an 𝐨𝐩𝐭𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐥 fact you can just see. 🔍 What we found: - 𝐍𝐞𝐚𝐫-𝐛𝐥𝐚𝐜𝐤 𝐧𝐨𝐧-𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐚𝐜𝐭 𝐩𝐢𝐱𝐞𝐥𝐬 (mean gray value < 3) alongside natural-looking contact pixels — robust to material, contact force, surface appearance, and lighting. - Over 𝟗𝟖% 𝐩𝐢𝐱𝐞𝐥-𝐥𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐥 𝐬𝐞𝐠𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐚𝐜𝐜𝐮𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐲 across diverse materials, with 𝐧𝐨 𝐦𝐢𝐧𝐢𝐦𝐮𝐦 𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐜𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐡𝐨𝐥𝐝. - Real manipulation tasks that force- and deformation-based sensors fail on: 𝐰𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐬𝐩𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠, 𝐟𝐚𝐜𝐢𝐚𝐥-𝐜𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐦 𝐝𝐢𝐩𝐩𝐢𝐧𝐠, and 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐧-𝐟𝐢𝐥𝐦 𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧. - Spatially aligned visual-tactile images that 𝐕𝐋𝐌𝐬 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐝 𝐝𝐢𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐥𝐲 — e.g., reasoning about resistor color codes for robotic sorting, with no extra calibration model in between. 🤖 Why it matters: as robots move from rigid pick-and-place into delicate, human-shared environments — food handling, skincare, healthcare — the bottleneck is no longer grip strength but 𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐜𝐞𝐢𝐯𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐥𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐭𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐭𝐨𝐮𝐜𝐡. Contact you can't sense is contact you can't control. This may trigger a new type of 𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐚 𝐜𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 for 𝐩𝐮𝐫𝐞𝐥𝐲 𝐯𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧-𝐛𝐚𝐬𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐥𝐞 𝐬𝐞𝐧𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐠. Because LightTact turns contact into something a camera can directly see, it can automatically stamp the very onset of touch — ground truth that ordinary cameras can then learn to perceive on their own. Paper: https://lnkd.in/gbBAWWFY Project: https://lnkd.in/gTUrNJ62 Code: https://lnkd.in/gipQWEEP This work is co-led by my students Changyi Lin and Boda Huo from Carnegie Mellon University . Thanks to our lab member Mingyang Yu , and collaborators Emily Ruppel , Bingqing Chen , and Jonathan Francis from Bosch . #Robotics #TactileSensing #TouchSensing #Sensors #RobotManipulation #DexterousManipulation #RobotLearning #EmbodiedAI #AI #Humanoids #RSS2026 #Carnegie Carnegie Mellon University #BoschAI

Soon people will realize that we need much more data than we initially thought to reach the “ChatGPT moment” for robots. One key category of missing data is touch. To understand contact-rich dexterous interaction, motion alone is not enough—we also need information about surface properties and contact states. Excited to share 𝐀𝐑𝐓-𝐆𝐥𝐨𝐯𝐞 🚀 , an articulated tactile glove that captures contact-grounded information while preserving full human dexterity. Led by my student Changyi Lin . What ART-Glove provides, all at once: - 𝐊𝐧𝐨𝐰𝐧 𝐠𝐞𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐭𝐫𝐲 — 16 rigid functional surfaces - 𝐒𝐮𝐫𝐟𝐚𝐜𝐞 𝐦𝐨𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 — 22 anatomically aligned joints - 𝐓𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐥𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐚𝐜𝐭 — 2,048 piezoresistive taxels Why this matters: teaching robots to manipulate the way people do requires demonstration data that is physically grounded — not just where the hand moved, but which surfaces touched what, and how. By combining known geometry, articulated motion, and dense tactile sensing in a wearable that doesn't sacrifice dexterity, 𝐀𝐑𝐓-𝐆𝐥𝐨𝐯𝐞 turns ordinary human hands into a rich source of contact-rich manipulation data. Huge congrats to Changyi Lin for leading this work, and thanks to Yuxiang Yang , Maria Bauza Villalonga , Maria Bauza Villalonga , and Peide Huang for the valuable advice and discussions. Paper: arxiv.org/abs/2606.16370 #Robotics #TactileSensing #DexterousManipulation #EmbodiedAI #CMU

Recently, I posted that current AI doesn't actually understand physical assets and homes. Here's what happens when it does. Rove deployed RapidEye across their luxury portfolio in NYC, the Hamptons, South Florida, and Aspen. Thousands of turnover photos flow through their Breezeway every week, RapidEye now reads and analyzes every one. The findings have been the kind of thing only an owner walking the property would catch. A pool umbrella that went missing between turnovers, surfaced by comparing one set of photos to the last. We've caught a thousand more like it. This is what Spatial Intelligence actually looks like in production and how it's changing the ops game for property management. If your team takes turnover photos, we can do the same for you. P.S. Rove has now switched many workflows to video inspections and is catching 4x more actionable findings. Shoot us a message if you're looking to transition to video for faster and more thorough inspections.
